A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same attack and theoretical contribution. The main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 Section 5 and Figure 1 report original simulated attacks on JL sketches using standard and noise-added estimators.

after.justification: V2 Section 5 and Figures 1–3 report original JL and AMS attack experiments, including repeated-trial results and confidence intervals.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 remains unchanged. However, Section 5 changes the stated sign rule in the simplified implementation: v1 compares the estimate with the query's actual norm, whereas v2 uses the fixed threshold sqrt(w²+1)=sqrt(2). This changes response generation within the implemented variant.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic norm-estimation task using a single-coordinate signal plus Gaussian noise. AMS introduces another sketch configuration, while varying ambient dimension changes experimental settings; neither introduces a separate dataset or task. Image classification remains discussion only.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates JL sketch-norm estimators and their Gaussian-noised variants. V2 retains these and adds the nonlinear AMS median-of-means estimator and its noised variants in Figure 2, expanding the evaluated responder families.

E3.justification: The empirical settings are substantially revised. V1's JL configurations (100,1000), (250,125000), and (1000,20000) are replaced by six JL configurations with smaller supports, alongside AMS experiments. V2 standardizes plots at 10,000 queries and uses noise scales {0,0.1,0.2,0.4}, replacing v1's longer runs and size-dependent noise grids.

E4.justification: V2 adds a controlled support-size sensitivity analysis through Figures 1 and 3, including n=500,1000,2000 at fixed k=250. This examines how noise support affects attack effectiveness beyond v1's existing sketch-size and robustness-noise comparisons.

E5.justification: V1 reports averages over 10 attacks for k=100,250 and three for k=1000, without confidence intervals. V2 reports 20 fresh-matrix trials per configuration and 95% confidence intervals throughout Figures 1–3, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V1's three JL result panels are replaced, and v2 adds AMS results and additional JL configurations. New findings include successful attacks with n/k between 2 and 5 and increasing JL attack effectiveness with larger support. The accuracy–robustness tradeoff persists, but changed settings prevent interpreting the new curves as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The attack guarantees, assumptions, lemmas, and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–E remain substantively unchanged. Removing a duplicate theorem restatement, numbering an existing distribution formula, and correcting notation and prose do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and central quadratic universal-attack claim are unchanged. The conclusion additionally highlights empirical compromise of the nonlinear AMS estimator and success with support as small as 2k, extending the stated empirical contribution without strengthening the theorem.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new experiments as evidence that practical vulnerability extends beyond the proved support requirements and optimal linear estimator. It connects support size to attacker storage and explicitly conjectures near-linear support suffices. The limitation against fully strategic responders is retained.

D1.justification: V2 specifies Gaussian JL entry variance, Rademacher AMS entries, median-of-means grouping formulas, fresh matrix sampling, and reuse of query vectors across noise levels. These improve implementation documentation; the more explicit JL distribution alone does not establish a change to v1's implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gribelyuk et al.'s Lifting Linear Sketches when discussing other norms and explicitly credits earlier single-batch attacks. It also connects future adaptive constructions to previously cited cardinality-sketch work. The additional Tricking the Hashing Trick bibliography entry duplicates an existing work.

P1.justification: Section 5 is reorganized into labeled estimator, attack, experiment, results, and discussion paragraphs, and the conclusion is rewritten. Local clarifications, acknowledgments, and removal of a repeated theorem statement accompany these changes; the overall theoretical and appendix structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The empirical display expands from one three-panel figure to three three-panel figures. V2 redraws the JL plots, adds AMS and support-size panels, and introduces confidence bands, reference lines, clearer ratio-axis labels, and more informative captions.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the empirical support more informative and assessable: confidence intervals over 20 trials replace averages alone, and AMS and support-size comparisons examine important applicability questions. These are useful gains over v1's JL demonstration, while the central theory and strategic-responder limitation remain unchanged. Different experimental settings preclude claiming a direct performance improvement.
